title: Rees deformation functoriality and the fixed-scheme inclusion
statement:
Let $X,X'$ be separated finite-type schemes over the algebraically closed field $k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be closed subschemes with ideals $I,J$, and let $f:X'\to X$ satisfy $f^{\cdot}I\,\mathcal O_{X'}\subseteq J$. Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$ as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Define the Rees deformation by
$$\widetilde X_Z=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{X_D}\bigl(\mathcal O_{X_D}[I/t]\bigr),$$
where the algebra is the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_{X_D}[t^{-1}]$ generated by $I/t$; define $\widetilde X'_{Z'}$ similarly. Its generic fibre is $X_\eta$, its special fibre is the normal cone $N_{Z/X}$ of [pur9-def-normal-cone], and the augmentation gives a closed zero section $Z_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z$. These are separated finite-type lifts. The map $f$ induces a unique lift $\widetilde f:\widetilde X'_{Z'}\to\widetilde X_Z$ over $f_D$. Its special fibre is the graded map $N_{Z'/X'}\to N_{Z/X}$ induced by $f^{\cdot}$.

The image of that special-fibre map is set-theoretically supported on the zero section if and only if $(f^{\cdot}I)^r\mathcal O_{X'}\subseteq J^{r+1}$ for some $r\geq1$. If $Z'=f^{-1}Z$ scheme-theoretically, the induced map $\widetilde X'_{Z'}\to\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$ is a closed immersion, and the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the zero section under the special-fibre map is exactly $Z'$.

For any correspondence $c:C\to X\times_kX$ of [def-trf-correspondence], put $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ and let $d:F\to X$ be the fixed-scheme projection of [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Applying the preceding construction to $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and the closed pair $Z\times Z\hookrightarrow X\times_kX$ gives the lifted correspondence
$$\widetilde c:\widetilde C_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)}\longrightarrow\widetilde X_Z\times_D\widetilde X_Z.$$
Writing $Z_F=d^{-1}(Z)$ and applying the same Rees construction to the closed pair $Z_F\hookrightarrow F$, the fixed-square relation gives a natural closed immersion
$$\widetilde F_{Z_F}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c).$$
On generic fibres this is the canonical identification with $\operatorname{Fix}(c)$.
